generations.description: The original WRX, legendary in rally and tuning culture. Featured turbocharged boxer engine and all-wheel drive. The STI variant with EJ20 engine became iconic.
First WRX sold in the US market. Featured 2.0L and 2.5L turbo engines. The STI model with 300+ horsepower became a tuner favorite and rally legend.
Wider body and improved handling. Featured EJ25 engine and continued the WRX's reputation for all-wheel-drive performance. STI model highly sought after.
Separated from Impreza platform. Featured FA20DIT engine producing 268 horsepower. Improved handling and technology while maintaining rally heritage.
Latest generation with FA24F engine producing 271 horsepower. Improved power delivery and handling. More refined while maintaining the WRX's character.
Subaru's rear-wheel-drive sports car co-developed with Toyota. Features naturally aspirated boxer engine, perfect weight distribution, and exceptional handling. Focus on driver engagement.
Refined second generation with improved 2.4L engine producing 228 horsepower. Better handling and technology while maintaining the BRZ's focus on pure driving experience.
Subaru's compact car platform that spawned the WRX. Featured all-wheel drive and boxer engines. The base for the legendary WRX STI variants.
Larger platform with improved safety and comfort. Featured updated engines and continued Subaru's focus on all-wheel drive and reliability.
More refined design with improved fuel economy. Featured updated boxer engines and continued Subaru's reputation for all-weather capability.
Complete redesign with improved technology and fuel economy. WRX separated to its own model. Focus on safety, reliability, and all-wheel-drive capability.
1st-gen Legacy sedan/wagon. Turbo EJ20T.
Subaru's mid-size sedan with all-wheel drive standard. Featured boxer engines and became known for reliability and all-weather capability.
Larger platform with improved interior space. Featured updated engines and continued Subaru's focus on safety and all-wheel drive.
More refined styling with improved technology. Featured updated boxer engines and introduced turbocharged option in GT trim.
Larger and more spacious with improved fuel economy. Featured updated engines and continued Legacy's reputation for reliability and all-weather capability.

Latest generation with improved technology and safety features. Featured updated boxer engines and continued Subaru's focus on all-wheel drive and reliability. Subaru announced the Legacy will be discontinued in the US after the 2025 model year.
First generation Forester XT with turbocharged EJ20 engine. Compact crossover with WRX-like performance. Popular in tuning community for its unique combination of utility and power.
Second generation with EJ25 turbo engine. Improved power and handling. STI variant available in some markets. Highly sought after by enthusiasts for its sleeper performance.
Third generation with EJ25 turbo producing 224-250 horsepower. More refined styling while maintaining performance. Popular platform for modifications and tuning.
Fourth generation with FA20DIT turbo engine producing 250 horsepower. Modern technology and improved fuel economy. Last generation with turbocharged XT variant in North America.
First generation Legacy GT with turbocharged EJ20 engine. Performance-oriented sedan and wagon variants. Established Legacy as a tuner-friendly platform.
Second generation with updated turbo engines. GT and GT-B variants offered increased performance. Popular for modifications and tuning.

Third generation Legacy GT with EJ255 turbo engine producing 243-265 horsepower. Spec.B variant with upgraded suspension and interior. Highly popular in tuning community for its balance of performance and practicality.
Fourth generation Legacy GT with EJ255 engine. Last generation with manual transmission option in North America. Sought after by enthusiasts for its combination of power and refinement.

Modern Legacy XT with FA24F turbo engine producing 260 horsepower. CVT-only transmission. Revived turbocharged Legacy for enthusiasts seeking performance in a refined package. Discontinued in the US after the 2025 model year alongside the rest of the Legacy lineup.
First generation Outback XT with EJ255 turbo engine producing 250 horsepower. Unique combination of crossover utility and turbocharged performance. Popular among enthusiasts for its versatility.

Second generation with EJ255 turbo engine. Improved styling and technology. Last generation with manual transmission option. Sought after for its rare combination of off-road capability and turbo power.
Modern Outback XT with FA24F turbo engine producing 260 horsepower and 277 lb-ft torque. CVT-only transmission. Revived turbocharged Outback offering performance in a practical crossover package.

Subaru's unique grand touring coupe with 3.3L flat-6 EG33 engine producing 230 horsepower. Distinctive styling with window-within-window design. Cult classic among enthusiasts for its rarity and character.

Subaru's futuristic coupe with wedge-shaped aerodynamic design. Featured EA82T turbo engine or ER27 flat-6 in XT6 variant. Unique pop-up headlights and advanced features. Rare enthusiast model with distinctive styling.
Subaru's three-row SUV on Global Platform. Turbocharged 2.4L FA24F. COBB Accessport support.
Outback-derived pickup. 2.5L NA / turbo.
First-generation Forester crossover SUV on the Impreza GC platform. Tall wagon body with all-wheel drive and naturally aspirated EJ25. Established Subaru's compact crossover segment in the US.
Second-generation Forester. Naturally aspirated EJ25 with optional XT turbo trim. Improved interior space and on-road refinement while keeping rugged AWD capability.
Third-generation Forester moved upmarket with a longer wheelbase and more carlike ride. EJ25 NA standard, EJ255 turbo on XT. Last generation with the high-roof boxy profile.
Fourth-generation Forester. NA FB25 standard, FA20DIT turbo on the XT trim. Modern interior with EyeSight driver assist on later years.
Fifth-generation Forester on the Subaru Global Platform. NA FB25 with CVT only. No turbo XT variant in the US for this generation.
First-generation Outback. Lifted Legacy wagon with two-tone paint and AWD. Created the rugged-wagon segment in the US.
Second-generation Outback on the Legacy BE/BH platform. Optional VDC stability control. H6-3.0 engine available on the L.L.Bean trim.
Third-generation Outback on the Legacy BL/BP platform. EJ253 H4 standard, EJ255 turbo on the Outback XT, EZ30 H6 on the 3.0R.
Fourth-generation Outback grew significantly with a higher roof and CVT-first powertrain. EJ253/FB25 H4 and EZ36 H6. XT turbo trim available early in the run.
Fifth-generation Outback. FB25 H4 and EZ36D H6 with CVT. EyeSight standard on later trims. No turbo variant in the US for this generation.
Sixth-generation Outback on the Subaru Global Platform. FB25 NA standard; FA24F turbo on the Outback XT and Wilderness trims.
First-generation Crosstrek (badged XV Crosstrek through 2015). Lifted Impreza GP/GJ five-door with cladding and AWD. FB20 NA only in the US; hybrid offered briefly mid-cycle.
Second-generation Crosstrek on the Subaru Global Platform. FB20 NA standard, FB25 added on later trims. Plug-in hybrid variant available 2019-2023 in select markets.
Third-generation Crosstrek with revised styling and a Wilderness trim. FB20 and FB25 NA powertrains; CVT only.
